old: This word traces back to a French verb meaning to settle something into a state of calm.
Its Middle English ancestor, apesen, meant to pacify or bring to peace.
The Old French root apeser is built around the very idea of "peace."
clues: This verb for dealing with someone's anger or demands traces back to an Old French word meaning to pacify, and it arrived in English already meaning to soothe.
It means calming someone by giving them what they want, more of a concession than simply soothing them. Critics use it for leaders who yield to aggressors to avoid conflict.
Ancient people did it to angry gods with offerings, and you can do it to your hunger with a snack. At its root, it means bringing someone peace.
